capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

- Represent \(p q\) by its prime factorization with multiplicity. Since \(p\) and \(q\) are prime, each contributes exactly one prime factor, and factorization is additive under multiplication. Thus \(pq\) has exactly two prime factors counted with multiplicity, even when \(p=q\), so it is \(2\)-almost-prime.

- For the spectral statement, use that `PrimeSpectrum.comap f` is monotone. Surjectivity of \(f\) makes contraction injective on ideals: for every ideal \(I\subseteq S\),
  \[
  \operatorname{map}_f(\operatorname{comap}_f I)=I.
  \]
  Hence equal contractions of two prime ideals imply the prime ideals themselves are equal. A monotone injective map between partial orders is strictly monotone: if \(P<Q\), their contractions are ordered and cannot be equal.

Surjectivity is the essential hypothesis in the second part; without it, distinct prime ideals can have the same contraction.
